title: FCRA — Adverse action notice requirement
description: The adverse-action notice obligation under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, applicable when a consumer report contributes to a credit or eligibility denial. Paraphrase pending verification against the primary statute text — hence 'Community' confidence.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content. Adverse-action notice obligations in the credit context arise under both FCRA (when a consumer report is used) and separately under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act/Regulation B (which requires reasons for credit denial regardless of report use); this control focuses on the FCRA-specific trigger, not the complete legal picture.

framework_name: Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), 15 U.S.C. § 1681 et seq.
control_text: When a creditor or other user of a consumer report takes adverse action based in whole or in part on information in that report — including reports or scores generated by algorithmic or AI-based systems — the user must provide the consumer an adverse action notice disclosing the action taken, the reporting agency used, and the consumer's rights, with a specific and accurate reason rather than a generic statement.

citations.title: Using Consumer Reports for Credit Decisions: What to Know About Adverse Action and Risk-Based Pricing Notices

relationships.reason: Satisfying this control requires a documented adverse-action notice record.
